Definition
[horosphere, asymptote]

Source: petersen:page-0317 ↗ def:pet-ch7-busemann-function The level sets $b_c^{-1}(t)$ are horospheres (hyperplanes in $\mathbb {R}^n$; spheres tangent to the boundary in the Poincaré model of hyperbolic space). Given a ray $c$ and $p\in M$, a family of unit-speed segments $\sigma _i:[0,L_i]\to M$ from $p$ to $c(t_i)$, $t_i\to \infty $, subconverges (as in subsection 3.1) to a ray $\tilde c:[0,\infty )\to M$, $\tilde c(0)=p$, called an asymptote for $c$ from $p$; asymptotes need not be unique.
